page: Microsoft Azure F48ams_v6 is a memory-intensive virtual server belonging to the Famsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores and 48 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core, with support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. The server is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, though it is premium storage capable for remote disk attachments.

In benchmark evaluations, the F48ams_v6 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU testing (147,761.02) and Geekbench multi-core scoring (24,166.0). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also reaches the top 10% tier at 626.48 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is strong across both cached small-block reads (7,120.47 GB/sec) and uncached large-block reads (226.16 GB/sec) and writes (144.16 GB/sec). For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier results in software compilation (65,929.0) and image processing (18,501.0), alongside strong performance in database operations (29,698.89) and Redis SET operations at 112.7 million operations per second. Large language model inference speeds are strong for small to medium models, though performance drops to average levels for larger 70B parameter models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the F48ams_v6 offers a high-density memory-to-CPU ratio combined with dedicated compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that still require robust parallel processing. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPU hardware represents a clear tradeoff, requiring reliance on network-attached premium storage and limiting its suitability for heavy GPU-accelerated deep learning. This server is best matched with memory-intensive applications, large-scale database operations, software compilation pipelines, and medium-scale LLM inference tasks.
